chunks.text: Her Career Conference 2026 — Her Future of Work (2nd Edition). Presented by Intelligent Nest and MamaNest. Main event: Saturday, May 30, 2026, 1:30 PM to 5:00 PM at District 3 Innovation Centre, 1250 Rue Guy Suite #600, Montreal, QC H3H 2L3. Workshop series: June 1-5, 2026, online. Registration: https://luma.com/qxt3t6an. Hashtag: #HerFutureOfWork.
Session 1: Registration & Networking. May 30, 2026, 1:30 PM. In-person at District3. 30 minutes.
Session 2: Welcome & Opening. Speaker: Lianna Della Vecchia. May 30, 2026, 2:00 PM. In-person at District3. 15 minutes.

Session 3: Opening Keynote | Intelligent Nest & MamaNest. Speaker: Mahsa Rezaei. May 30, 2026, 2:15 PM. In-person at District3. 30 minutes. The future of work conversation has a problem: it keeps asking women to adapt to a world that was never designed for them.
The World Economic Forum says 39% of core skills will shift by 2030. The Anthropic Labour Market Report signals the biggest workforce transformation of the century. UNESCO warns that women remain underrepresented in AI — limiting their influence over how this transformation unfolds.
But here's what the data doesn't say loudly enough: the skills that will matter most — adaptability, relational intelligence, navigating complexity, building community under pressure, holding multiple roles simultaneously — are skills women have been developing their entire lives. Without a title. Without recognition. Without being paid what they're worth.
The future of work isn't coming for women. It's arriving, and women are already holding the map.
In this keynote, Future of Work Architect and TEDx Speaker Mahsa Rezaei draws on original research, 15 years of ecosystem building, and the launch of Canada's first AI career platform built specifically for women — to present a new framework for career reinvention in the age of AI. Part research session, part manifesto, part live demonstration: this is not another inspiration talk. It's a strategy for winning — on your own terms, in a world you were always meant to help build.
Session 4: Speed Networking Activity. Speaker: Jeffrey To. May 30, 2026, 2:45 PM. In-person at District3. 30 minutes.
Session 5: Networking Break. May 30, 2026, 3:15 PM. In-person at District3. 15 minutes.

Session 6: Panel Discussion — Women, Work & What’s Next: Navigating the Future of Work. Speaker: Lin Sok, Dominique Pirolo, Samantha Bateman, Rachel Beyerlein. May 30, 2026, 3:30 PM. In-person at District3. 60 minutes. The future of work is being shaped by AI, automation, and evolving hiring systems—but not all voices are being considered equally.
For many women—especially those navigating career gaps, transitions, or systemic barriers—the question isn’t just how to adapt… it’s how to stay visible, relevant, and competitive in a system that wasn’t designed with them in mind.
In this bold and honest conversation, our panelists will unpack:
What’s actually broken in today’s hiring and workplace systems
How AI and data are reshaping opportunity—and bias
What women need to understand now to stay ahead
And most importantly, how to position yourself to win—on your own terms.
This is not another “inspiration” panel.
It’s a reality check—and a strategy session.

Session 7: Closing Keynote. Speaker: Stefania Pecore. May 30, 2026, 4:30 PM. In-person at District3. 20 minutes. Everyone’s talking about AI. Most people are using it to do the same thing they’ve always done: just faster. That’s not a strategy. That’s duct tape.
The professionals who will actually pull ahead are the ones who develop the habit underneath the tool: the ability to observe how they work,
test small changes, learn from the results, and build something repeatable. That habit is what makes AI useful.
Without it, you’re just prompting into the void.
In this session, Ysi —founder of Vantelira Inc. and former Fortune 500 supply chain leader — gives you the operator’s lens, applied to your own career.
You’ll learn how to map what you’re already doing, run small experiments on the parts that matter most,
and turn what works into a repeatable process that AI can actually support.
This isn’t a job search tutorial. It’s the thinking skill that makes every next tool and every next career move easier to navigate.
Session 8: Closing Remarks, Award, Group photo. May 30, 2026, 4:50 PM. In-person at District3. 15 minutes.
